newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Armed forces officials warned the Moro National Liberation Front that the reported recruitment of new rebels to qualify for integration with the military and police could be a violation of the peace agreement. (TODAY)

- At a Senate hearing on the proposed 1997 budget for the Office of the President, Executive Secretary Ruben Torres said Ramos plans to go on an 11-country tour next year "to meet international commitments and reciprocate visits by other leaders."

- Malacanang palace assured Communist Party of the Philippines leader Jose Maria Sison, who lives in exile in the Netherlands, that he would not be arrested should he return home anytime this year. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- President Ramos allayed fears over the proposed national identity system, saying it has nothing to do with a perceived return to dictatorial or military rule. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- President Ramos shot down the proposed barangay (village) identity card system even as mayors and barangay officials nationwide rallied behind the proposal of Interior and Local Government Secretary Robert Barbers. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Australian telecommunications firms ADI Ltd, John Holland Construction and MM Cables Communication are arriving in Manila on September 30 along with seven other firms to explore opportinities for supply-contract deals with Filipino companies. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- The combined remittances of the country's 4.2 million overseas contract workers are projected to reach at least $7 billion by the end of the year, according to the Central Bank (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
